nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذا is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative by جاء. نَصْرُ اللَّهِ is nominative by جاء (as its agent); (نصر) has the plural anṣār, and by analogy (it should be) anṣur. وَالْفَتْحُ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ: «يدخلون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or as the predicate (second object) of رأيت. أَفْواجاً is accusative as a ḥāl, the plural of fawj; by analogy, fawj (should have the plural) afwuj, but the vowel on the wāw was felt to be heavy, so they likened faʿl to fiʿl [Translator's note: i.e., gave it the plural pattern afʿāl].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ, i.e., make your glorification with praise. وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ: and he ﷺ used to say: «I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times in the day and the night». إِنَّهُ كانَ تَوَّاباً: (توابا is) the khabar (predicate) of كان, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. There was in this sūra an indication of his prophethood ﷺ, because it was revealed before the Conquest. Ibn ʿAbbās said: so he knew that when the Conquest came… so we counted (it as a sign of) his appointed term ﷺ [Translator's note: the sentence is disjointed in the text]. Qatāda said: the sūra of the Conquest, إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ, was revealed in Medina.
